front.title: Adaptive Load Balancing for Equal-Cost Multipath (ECMP)

abstract.t: Equal-Cost Multipath (ECMP) forwarding assigns a flow to a next-hop by computing a hash over packet header fields when the flow is first seen. Because the assignment does not change after that, the load across the paths of an ECMP group can become uneven when the set of paths changes or when traffic shifts among existing flows. This document defines procedures for adaptive ECMP load balancing in which a forwarding node periodically measures per-path load, determines whether the load is sufficiently uneven to act on, and makes a bounded number of incremental flow placement changes toward less-used paths. The procedures preserve per-flow packet ordering for all but the small number of flows that are moved in any interval, and they converge toward a balanced distribution across the group. The procedures operate within a single forwarding node and add no new packet formats or inter-node signaling.
